steps.reason: Scope the dataset before any computation. No time/amount/account filters specified, so full dataset is used.

Layering typically involves rapid movement of funds and high velocity. Per-account rolling features (especially rapid in->out ratio and velocity) are required inputs for the rules engine and anomaly model.
Layering manifests as rapid_movement (funds quickly passed through accounts), velocity spikes, and potentially structuring to obscure amounts. Rules engine flags accounts matching these patterns.
Layering is a broad 'find anything suspicious' concern — anomaly model catches accounts whose behavior deviates from the population baseline in ways rules alone might miss.
Layering inherently involves a network of accounts passing funds through multiple hops. Graph analysis is essential to detect ring structures and short cycles characteristic of layering.
Combines rule hits, anomaly scores, and graph findings into a final LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH risk ranking per account so analysts can prioritize reviews.
